Measured independently at the merged head 0559eb35, by this reviewer:

The inversion is gone as behaviour, not as a rename. The first implementation (d21b09d7) had no prescription branch at all: its verdict was margin >= 0 -> send, margin >= -0.15 -> split, else hold, and its own gate asserted the inverted policy at tests/test_bar.py:90-91 of that commit -- recommend(1.0, 0.0).verdict == HOLD and recommend(1.0, 1.0).verdict == SEND. Swept over the same 21x21 (fill, score) grid, the two modules disagree on 322 of 441 cells (73%), and both named points have flipped: (fill 1.0, score 0.0) hold -> send-local, (fill 1.0, score 1.0) send -> hold. Restoring the first implementation's policy into the delivered module reddens tests/test_bar.py::test_send_local_is_returned_at_its_own_boundary, ::test_all_four_outcomes_are_reachable_and_distinct, ::test_a_maximally_prescribed_node_is_never_held_at_any_fill and ::test_hold_is_decided_by_the_score_with_the_fill_held_constant (4 failed, 15 passed), so the defect cannot be reintroduced without the gate reporting it.

Hold is decided by the score at a fixed fill, and its reachability has a fill floor. Holding the fill at 0.85 and sweeping only the score (101 samples), hold spans scores 0.26-0.78 and is absent at both ends; no fill in the 21-point grid holds every sampled score, because a score at or below PRESCRIBED_MAX is send-local at any fill. Hold first becomes reachable at fill >= 0.435, where the bar reads 0.403 -- below that the window has too much room for a prescribed-above node to be refused, which is the bar being a function of window state at all, as the section requires. At a full window the vertex is missed: scores 0.90 and 0.95 are split while 1.00 is held, so the score axis is non-monotone in the last band.
